name: authors-structure-domain
description: Boundaries, domains and system structure. No text reused.

rules.title: Service boundaries follow bounded contexts
rules.requirement: Each service owns a coherent part of the domain with its own model and language, and the design names the contexts and how terms are translated at their borders.

source.name: Eric Evans
source.locator: Domain-Driven Design, Chapter 14, Maintaining Model Integrity

rules.title: Each piece of data has exactly one owning service
rules.requirement: No two services write the same table or record. The design names the owner of each data set and how other services obtain copies or ask for changes.

source.name: Sam Newman
source.locator: Building Microservices, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, Microservice Communication Styles, and Chapter 6, Workflow

rules.title: Distribution is justified, not assumed
rules.requirement: For each network boundary introduced, the design states the benefit that outweighs the added latency, failure modes and operational cost, since the first rule of distributed objects is not to distribute them.

source.name: Martin Fowler
source.locator: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, Chapter 7, Distribution Strategies

rules.title: Migrations use incremental replacement with a kill switch
rules.requirement: Where an existing system is replaced, traffic is moved in slices behind a facade or router, each slice can be reverted independently, and the old path is retired only after the new one has proven itself.

rules.title: Architecture characteristics are ranked and traded explicitly
rules.requirement: The document ranks the characteristics that matter most for this system, such as availability, elasticity, security and evolvability, and the decisions reference that ranking when they trade one against another.

source.name: Mark Richards and Neal Ford
source.locator: Fundamentals of Software Architecture, Chapters 4 to 6, Architecture Characteristics

rules.title: Diagrams use consistent abstraction levels with a legend
rules.requirement: Each diagram sits at one level, such as system context, containers or components, mixes no levels, and has a legend or consistent notation for boxes and lines.
